inputs.base_revenue_note: TTM to 30-Jun-2026 = FY2025 22,669 + H1-2026 13,425 - H1-2025 10,327. FY0 is the trailing twelve months ending on the balance-sheet date so that H1-2026 cash (already inside the 30-Jun-26 cash balance) is not counted again in Y1. Y1 = Jul-2026..Jun-2027.
inputs.share_count_basis: Cover-page common shares 1,053.7M at 2026-07-16 (Q2 2026 10-Q, dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding) plus ~2M dilutive awards (Q2 2026 diluted 1,067M less basic 1,065M weighted average). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows; buybacks (US$3.46B in H1-2026, >100M shares retired since Feb-2024) are the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat and are value-neutral here. ~$0.6B of July-2026 repurchases are already inside the 16-Jul count but were funded from the 30-Jun cash; immaterial against a $9.0B cash balance.
inputs.net_debt_note: Company definition at 30-Jun-2026: Debt 5,083 + Lease and other financing obligations 515 - Cash 9,009 = net cash 3,411 (Q2 2026 release, Net Debt reconciliation). Leases treated as debt (treatment A); operating-lease cost is already inside OCF/EBITDA.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: TTM to 30-Jun-2026 company-definition FCF (OCF less additions to PP&E and mine development): OCF 12,628 (10,334 + 6,709 - 4,415) less capex 2,895 (3,035 + 1,360 - 1,500).
inputs.interest_income_note: TTM investment income 214 (FY2025) + 171 (H1-2026) - 95 (H1-2025) = 290; stripped because net cash is added to EV in the bridge and the model is unlevered (interest expense ~$175M/yr guided is likewise excluded).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement share-based compensation $99M (XBRL AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense) plus $23M cash tax withholding on net-share settlement (PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation); no combined figure published, so the two are summed; rounded to $120M for the TTM base (H1-2026 SBC not separately tagged).
inputs.buyback_cash_note: H1-2026 repurchases of common stock $3,462M (FY2025 $2,303M). $4.3B remained under the $6.0B authorization at 23-Jul-2026. Real financing outflow, not an authorization.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built: 10y UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.0 = ~9.2% cost of equity; $5.1B of fixed-rate debt at ~5% pre-tax against a ~$121B market cap is <5% of capital, so WACC rounds to 9.0%. Used in all three scenarios: commodity-price risk is charged once, in the scenario price decks and weights, not again in the discount rate (adaptations section f).
inputs.lease_treatment: A: leases as debt. Lease and other financing obligations ($515M at 30-Jun-26) added to debt in the bridge; operating-lease expense remains inside EBITDA; no separate lease_cost_pct_path.
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only flows. Merian (25% Staatsolie) NCI took $82M of FY2025 profit and $115M of H1-2026; folded into the cash tax rate as ~1.5pp of leakage on top of the 33% guided adjusted tax rate (34.5% all-in). NCI book value ($171M) is NOT deducted in the bridge, so it is charged once.
inputs.equity_affiliates_treatment: Pueblo Viejo (40%) and Lundin Gold / Fruta del Norte (32%) are equity-method and are EXCLUDED from revenue and adjusted EBITDA (the company's adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation strips equity income), so their distributions ($193M in Q2 2026) are not in the projected flows; the stakes are added in equity_bridge instead (matching-asset rule). Nevada Gold Mines (38.5%) is proportionately consolidated and IS in the flows.
inputs.reclamation_treatment: Reclamation and remediation liabilities ($6,513M ARO at 30-Jun-26) are NOT deducted as debt. Cash reclamation spend ($803M FY2025, $458M H1-2026, vs ~$385M/yr accretion) is charged inside the cash-EBITDA margin (~1.5-2pp below the company's adjusted EBITDA margin). Charging both would double-count.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF on a MID-CYCLE commodity price deck (routing: operating company, cyclical -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md; same family as BSL.AX, CMM.AX, FMG.AX, HAL). Newmont is the world's largest gold producer (5.26 Moz attributable 2026 guide, by-product AISC $1,680/oz) with copper/silver/lead/zinc co-products; a pure price-taker, so the valuation is a gold price deck first and an operating model second. Trailing numbers are NOT a clean run-rate: TTM realized gold ~$4,270/oz (spot $4,350 on 2026-10-01; Jan-2026 peak ~$5,590) against a 5-year average near $2,800, so the base case normalizes gold to $3,800/oz by Y2 and grows it with inflation (2.5%), the bull holds $4,500-4,700 and compounds 3%/yr, the bear reverts to $2,800 (the 5-yr average). H1-2026 was also depressed by the April-2026 Cadia seismic event (copper -43%, co-product volumes -22..-35% QoQ) and FY2025 includes ~$975M of divestiture gains and ~$4.3B of asset-sale proceeds that are excluded here. Revenue is built as consolidated gold ounces sold (~5.1-5.25 Moz; 5.26 Moz attributable guide less ~0.45 Moz equity-method PV/FDN ounces, plus Merian NCI ounces) x gold deck + co-product revenue ($3.0-3.8B/yr depending on copper/silver). Cash cost base ~$9.4B TTM (CAS ~$8.2B incl. NGM share, G&A $375M, exploration $525M, cash reclamation ~$650M, other) inflated at 3%/yr with royalty relief of ~$6/oz per $100/oz of gold; this gives cash-EBITDA margins that reconcile to OCF + cash taxes + interest, ~1.5-2pp below the company's adjusted EBITDA margin (TTM adjusted EBITDA $16,765M = 65.1%). Capex = sustaining $1.95B + development $1.4B (2026 guide; capitalized interest excluded); D&A guided $2,815M for 2026 and converges toward capex. Cash tax 33% guided adjusted rate + 1.5pp NCI leakage. Terminal cap 12x owner FCF (cyclical, depleting reserves; HAL/BSL precedent) binds in every scenario against Gordon at 9%/2.5%. Buybacks: the company IS a repurchaser ($3.46B H1-2026), so the flat count is funded. Historical CAGRs (revenue 14.5% 5yr, 23.9% 3yr) are price- and Newcrest-driven and are not used as a growth anchor; selected_growth_rate is the terminal nominal price-inflation rate.

equity_bridge.item: Lundin Gold 32% equity-method stake (Fruta del Norte)
equity_bridge.note: ~77M LUG.TO shares x C$86.69 (Yahoo, 2026-10-01) x CAD/USD 0.7031 = ~US$4.7B at market; taken at a 20% haircut for consistency with the base $3,800/oz deck. Stake's equity income/distributions are excluded from the flows.

Approximately carrying value (total equity-method investments $3,708M at 30-Jun-26 less the Lundin Gold carrying amount); Q2 2026 distributions $100M against $32M expansion contributions. Not in the flows.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: mid-cycle price deck: terminal nominal gold-price inflation; historical CAGRs are gold-price and Newcrest-acquisition artefacts for a price-taker
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 7.4% vs revenue 5yr CAGR 14.5% (>30% divergence): revenue growth FY2020-25 is realized gold price ($1,775 -> ~$3,400/oz) plus the Nov-2023 all-stock Newcrest acquisition (shares 806M -> 1,152M), not organic volume. 3yr figures (FY2022 base) start from a trough year with -$429M net income. EPS 3yr CAGR undefined (FY2022 EPS -0.54).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC incl. withholding - interest income): FY2020 3,424; FY2021 2,511; FY2022 896; FY2023 -156; FY2024 2,706; FY2025 6,963; TTM Jun-2026 9,323. FY2023 includes Newcrest transaction costs and the Penasquito strike. Owner-FCF and reported-FCF CAGRs are close because SBC (~0.5% of revenue) is immaterial; interest income ($290M TTM) is the larger adjustment.

base.growth_rationale: Gold $4,100 avg in Y1 (spot $4,350 drifting to ~$3,900 by mid-2027) x 5.1 Moz consolidated + co-products $3.4B = ~$24.3B; Y2 gold $3,800 x 5.2 Moz + $3.1B = ~$22.9B; Y3 $3,850 x 5.25 Moz (Cadia fully recovered, Tanami 2 ramping) = ~$23.4B; thereafter +2.5%/yr nominal price inflation on flat volumes (the Feb-2026 framework targets per-share, not absolute, production growth; depletion offsets panel-cave growth).
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: Cash-EBITDA basis (reconciles to OCF + cash taxes + interest; includes cash reclamation spend; excludes equity income and interest income). Cash cost base ~$9.6B Y1 (TTM ~$9.4B +3% inflation, less ~$0.14B royalty relief at lower gold), ~$9.9B Y2, then +3%/yr against +2.5% revenue, so margin drifts ~0.25pp/yr lower. TTM comparable ~62%.
base.da_rationale: 2026 guide $2,815M (~11.7% of Y1 revenue); converges toward the capex ratio as the post-Newcrest asset base depreciates.
base.capex_rationale: Sustaining $1.95B + development $1.4B = $3.35B (2026 guide, ex capitalized interest) on Y1 revenue; ~$3.3B held in dollars through the Y2 price dip, then ~13.5% (~$3.2-3.8B) for reserve replacement and tailings.
base.cash_tax_rationale: 33% guided adjusted tax rate (income + mining taxes across Australia, Ghana, PNG, Mexico, Peru, Suriname, US) + ~1.5pp Merian NCI leakage. FY2025 cash taxes paid 2,458 were 21.7% of pretax because of payment lag; H1-2026 cash taxes 2,349 = 31% of pretax.
base.narrative: Gold normalizes rather than collapses: the central-bank bid persists but the 2024-26 premium fades, with the price settling near $3,800/oz by Y2 and inflating 2.5%/yr thereafter. Newmont holds ~5.1-5.25 Moz of consolidated production, Cadia recovers from the April-2026 seismic event, and by-product AISC sits around $1,700-1,900/oz as inflation and lower co-product credits offset royalty relief. Owner FCF of ~$6-7.5B/yr funds the $1.1B dividend and ratable buybacks; the 12x cap binds the terminal value.

bull.growth_rationale: Gold $4,500 Y1 (guidance deck) and $4,700 Y2, then +3%/yr; copper $11,000/t and silver $60 hold; volumes +1%/yr as Cadia panel caves, Tanami Expansion 2 and Lihir/Cerro Negro extensions deliver. Y1 ~$26.9B, Y2 ~$28.5B.
bull.ebitda_margin_rationale: Same ~$9.7B/$10.0B cash cost base as the base case (royalties ~$0.1B higher at higher gold) against higher revenue; +4% revenue vs +3% costs lifts margin ~0.3pp/yr.
bull.capex_rationale: ~$3.5B Y1 (development accelerates with the price), then 12.5% of a larger revenue base (~$3.6-4.9B) funding growth projects.
bull.narrative: The structural gold bull market continues: central banks keep buying ~70t/month, real rates fall as the Fed eventually eases, and gold holds $4,500-4,700/oz and compounds with inflation. Copper stays above $10,000/t on the electrification deficit and silver stays elevated, so Peñasquito and Cadia by-product credits keep AISC near $1,600/oz. Newmont converts record margins into owner FCF of $9-14B/yr, executes the full $6B buyback and successive authorizations, and the Tier 1 portfolio adds ~1%/yr of ounces. Even here the terminal value is capped at 12x.

bear.growth_rationale: Hawkish-Fed / safe-haven unwind: gold averages $3,300 in Y1 on the way to $2,800 (the 5-year average) in Y2, then +2%/yr; co-products weak ($2.6-2.9B); volumes 5.0 Moz with Cadia slower to recover. Y1 ~$19.6B, Y2 ~$16.6B.
bear.ebitda_margin_rationale: Cash costs are sticky: ~$9.5B Y1 (royalty relief ~$0.3B) and ~$9.6B Y2 against sharply lower revenue; thereafter +3% costs vs +2% revenue erodes ~0.4pp/yr. By-product AISC ~$1,900-2,100/oz as co-product credits shrink.
bear.da_rationale: D&A stays ~$2.7-2.8B in dollars (depreciation of the Newcrest asset base does not fall with the gold price) on a smaller revenue base.
bear.capex_rationale: Development capex cut to ~$0.6B but sustaining capex (~$1.95B incl. tailings) is non-discretionary: ~$2.9B Y1, ~$2.6B Y2, then ~15% of revenue.
bear.narrative: The 2024-26 gold premium unwinds: the Fed stays hawkish into 2027, real yields rise, central-bank accumulation slows and ETF/safe-haven flows reverse, taking gold back to its 5-year average near $2,800/oz. Newmont's largely fixed per-ounce cost base and sticky sustaining capex compress owner FCF to ~$3B/yr; development projects are deferred, the $6B buyback slows to the dividend, and a jurisdictional shock (Ghana/PNG royalty push, a Merian or Peñasquito labor stoppage) removes ounces at the worst time. Net cash and the equity-method stakes cushion the balance sheet; there is no solvency question, only a much lower earnings base.

scenario_narratives.base: Gold normalizes to ~$3,800/oz by Y2 (down ~13% from $4,350 spot, still ~35% above the 5-year average) and inflates 2.5%/yr; Newmont holds ~5.1-5.25 Moz consolidated with Cadia recovered, cash-EBITDA margins ~55-57%, owner FCF ~$6-7.5B/yr, 12x terminal cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: Gold holds $4,500-4,700/oz and compounds 3%/yr with copper and silver strong; volumes +1%/yr from Cadia panel caves and Tanami 2; margins 64-67%; owner FCF $9-14B/yr.
scenario_narratives.bear: Gold reverts to the 5-year average $2,800/oz by Y2 on a hawkish Fed and a safe-haven unwind; sticky costs and sustaining capex compress owner FCF to ~$3B/yr; margins ~39-42%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 15/50/35 moved to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25% because gold trades at ~1.6x its 5-year average after a 2024-26 run driven by central-bank and safe-haven demand that has already partly unwound (Jan-2026 $5,590 -> $4,350), and a price-taker with fixed per-ounce costs has no lever against it; the balance sheet (net cash $3.4B) removes solvency from the bear case but not earnings risk. Bull cut to 25% because it requires gold to hold record levels AND copper/silver to stay elevated AND three growth projects to deliver on time. Base is a genuine normalization, not spot.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Newmont is valued as a mid-cycle owner-FCF stream, not on trailing numbers. The TTM to June 2026 (revenue $25.8B, owner FCF $9.3B) was earned at ~$4,270/oz gold, double the 5-year average, with FY2025 further flattered by ~$1B of divestiture gains; none of that is carried forward. Each scenario is a gold price deck applied to ~5.1-5.25 Moz of consolidated ounces on a cash cost base of ~$9.4-10B that inflates 3%/yr, with sustaining capex treated as non-discretionary. SBC (~0.5% of revenue) is expensed and the 1,056M diluted count held flat; interest income is stripped and net cash ($3.4B incl. leases) plus the equity-method stakes (Lundin Gold at a haircut to market, Pueblo Viejo near book) are added in the bridge; NCI is charged as tax leakage; reclamation is charged in the flows. One 9% USD WACC for all scenarios with risk carried in the decks and 25/50/25 weights; a 12x cap on terminal FCF binds everywhere.
key_risks_to_valuation: Gold price deck: every $100/oz on ~5.1 Moz is ~$0.5B of revenue and ~$0.3B of owner FCF, roughly $3-4/share of value at a 12x cap; the base $3,800 deck is a judgment between spot ($4,350) and the 5-year average ($2,800).
Co-product prices (copper, silver, lead, zinc ~$3-3.8B of revenue) move AISC by-product credits by hundreds of dollars per ounce.
Cost inflation and currency: AUD, CAD, MXN, PGK, GHS cost bases against USD revenue; a weaker dollar lifts AISC.
Operational and jurisdictional shocks: Cadia seismic recovery, Peñasquito labor, Ghana/PNG/Suriname royalty and permitting regimes.
Reserve replacement: production is modelled flat in the base; failure to replace ~5 Moz/yr of depletion would lower the terminal value, which is 12x capped and ~45% of EV.
Reclamation: $6.5B of ARO is charged through cash spend inside the margin (~$650M/yr); Yanacocha water-treatment estimates have been revised upward before.
Equity-method stakes in the bridge ($6.1B, ~$5.8/share) are marked off a 32% Lundin Gold holding at a haircut to a market price that itself embeds $4,350 gold.
